claim: A population or opponent read must remain attached to the action branch that generated it; global labels are weaker than position-, action-, size- and line-specific evidence.
interpretation: The trainer should store the observed node and consequence rather than convert one tendency into a universal player type.
assumptions: The observation can be tied to a concrete decision branch
Different branches can contain different range construction
exceptions: A global shorthand is acceptable only after multiple branch observations support it
notes: Evidence changes exploit weighting, not source truth.

claim: A single showdown can establish that a hand-line combination exists but cannot by itself establish its frequency or justify a high-confidence population magnitude.
interpretation: One observation should create a note or low-confidence hypothesis, not an automatic range rewrite or universal exploit.
assumptions: Only one relevant observation is available
No independent sample establishes the frequency
exceptions: A single observation can still disprove an absolute claim that the line is impossible
notes: Epistemic guardrail, not a statistical sample-size theorem.

claim: Source-backed population tendencies may guide attention before a local sample exists, but their magnitude must remain uncertain until the target environment or opponent provides supporting evidence.
interpretation: Use a structural baseline plus a low-confidence prior; do not present source population claims as proven Batumi frequencies.
assumptions: The target pool has not yet been directly validated
exceptions: Repeated local evidence can increase confidence and exploit weighting

claim: Field evidence may change priority, exploit weighting and exception prominence but must not silently rewrite an admitted source claim or unresolved theoretical boundary.
interpretation: Observed hands refine the environment model while preserving the distinction between theory, inference and field calibration.
assumptions: The project distinguishes source claims from field observations
Field notes can be reviewed and scoped
exceptions: Enough new evidence can trigger a formal claim re-review through the admission process
